Sun|Sun.fused: Both of them build a sense of self out of the same raw material. Recognition is instant — the same things make them proud, the same slights sting. The risk is a shared blind spot: nobody is standing at a different angle to catch what they both miss.
Sun|Sun.easy: They want to be seen for similar things without wanting the same spotlight, so encouragement costs them nothing. It comes so cheaply it can go unsaid for years. Worth putting into words now and then, or it stops registering at all.
Sun|Sun.friction: They respect each other and still keep pressing the wrong button — the thing one is proudest of is the thing the other quietly finds overdone. It rarely explodes; it leaks out as small corrections and faint sighs. It settles when each stops hearing the other's way of being as a comment on their own.
Sun|Sun.facing: Each is strong exactly where the other is thin, which is why they hold each other's attention. The pull is real and so is the gap: what one calls confidence, the other calls performance, and the reverse is equally true. Handled well it is a genuine trade; handled badly it becomes a scoreboard.

Moon|Sun.fused: What one of them simply is, the other finds comforting — being near them is restful without anyone trying. The catch is dependence: safety gets built on one person carrying on being themselves, so a bad week for them becomes a bad week for both.
Moon|Sun.easy: One person's ordinary way of going about things happens to steady the other. Reassurance arrives without being asked for, which is lovely and easy to stop noticing. Neither should assume the supply is automatic.
Moon|Sun.friction: The thing one of them is most sure about is the thing that leaves the other faintly unsettled — certainty heard as pressure, or steadiness heard as dullness. It shows up in small domestic moments rather than big arguments. Saying the need plainly, instead of hinting, is what breaks the loop.
Moon|Sun.facing: One reaches outward to know who they are, the other reaches inward to feel calm, and each is drawn to what they lack. The same free evening looks like an opportunity to one and a retreat to the other. The tension is workable; pretending it is not there is not.

Mercury|Sun.fused: One person's way of talking runs on the same track as the other's sense of self, so conversation feels like being understood without translation. The danger is that agreement gets mistaken for accuracy — nobody in the room is checking the reasoning.
Mercury|Sun.easy: One explains, the other is confirmed, and talk quietly does the work of steadying who they are. Praise lands well and criticism is heard as help rather than attack. Because none of it takes effort, real disagreement can stay unspoken far too long.
Mercury|Sun.friction: The pace, the jokes, the endless qualifying — the way one talks keeps grazing the other's dignity. It surfaces as arguments about tone rather than substance, the "that is not what I said" kind. Slowing down and repeating the other's point back defuses most of it.
Mercury|Sun.facing: One knows what they are; the other wants to turn it over from the far side. That makes for genuinely good conversation and genuine needling, because a question can land as doubt. It works while questions stay questions and do not harden into cross-examination.

Sun|Venus.fused: Affection here lands precisely on what the other most wants to be recognised for, so being loved and being seen are the same event. The risk is that warmth slides into flattery, and neither can tell any more whether the other means it.
Sun|Venus.easy: The way one shows care fits the other's sense of self with no adjusting — the right compliment, the right small gift, without study. It is pleasant enough to become the whole relationship. Worth checking occasionally that the warmth is doing more than decorating.
Sun|Venus.friction: One person's affection arrives in a form the other cannot quite accept: too much, too public, or aimed at a version of them they do not recognise. It repeats as awkwardness around gestures, gifts and anniversaries. It eases when the giver asks what actually feels good rather than what ought to.
Sun|Venus.facing: Real magnetism, because each finds something in the other they cannot produce themselves. But one wants to be admired and the other wants to admire, and those roles chafe if they never swap. Expect attraction with an undertow of wanting things on your own terms.

Mars|Sun.fused: Drive and identity fire together: when one goes after something, the other feels it as a matter of who they are. Huge momentum, short fuse. Arguments escalate fast because a disagreement about a plan lands as an insult.
Mars|Sun.easy: One person's push and the other's sense of self point the same way, so getting things done together is unusually simple and competition stays sporting. The hazard is coasting — nobody pushes hard enough to find out what they could actually do.
Mars|Sun.friction: The bluntness and pace of one keeps landing on the other's pride. It returns to the same subject every time: who decided, who moved first, who was consulted. Agreeing how a decision gets made, before there is one to make, does more than any apology.
Mars|Sun.facing: Attraction across a real divide — one is pulled towards the other's directness and braced against it at the same time. Fights are frequent, honest, and not always harmful. It stays healthy while the aim is to settle the thing rather than to win it.

Jupiter|Sun.fused: One person's optimism is fastened straight onto the other's sense of self, so encouragement is constant and generous. Everything looks bigger than it is. Someone outside this pair should be checking the numbers.
Jupiter|Sun.easy: The belief that things will work out lands on the other exactly where they need backing, and they never have to ask for it. Confidence grows on both sides. Because it is easy, promises get made more freely than they get kept.
Jupiter|Sun.friction: One person's cheerfulness reads as not taking the other seriously; the other's caution reads as sulking. It surfaces whenever money or plans come up. Concrete figures, rather than mood, are what settle it.
Jupiter|Sun.facing: One holds the position, the other holds the horizon, and each thinks the other overdoes it. The pull is genuine — it is a relief to be pushed to expand, and a relief to be pulled back to earth. Trouble starts when either treats the other's setting as a character flaw.

Saturn|Sun.fused: Seriousness and identity sit on the same spot, so the relationship has weight from the beginning and neither takes it lightly. It also means criticism cuts straight to the core, and going quiet is not a mood but a shutdown. Durable, but lightness has to be added on purpose.
Saturn|Sun.easy: One's steadiness gives the other something to lean on: commitments get kept, and structure is welcome rather than resented. This kind ages well. The cost is a certain flatness — neither is likely to surprise the other.
Saturn|Sun.friction: One person's standards keep landing on the other as disapproval, whether or not that was meant. It comes back around obligations, deadlines and family expectations. It improves when the serious one says out loud what they do admire, because silence gets heard as judgement.
Saturn|Sun.facing: A real pull between wanting to be seen and wanting to be sound. One warms the room, the other checks the exits, and each finds the other both necessary and exasperating. If going cold becomes the standard answer to conflict, the gap widens fast.

Sun|Uranus.fused: The need for room and the sense of self are the same thing here, so being told who to be lands as being told to stop existing. Together they change plans often and enjoy it. Routine is the thing most likely to break them.
Sun|Uranus.easy: One person's independence does not threaten the other's footing, so space gets given without a negotiation. Neither has to explain a night alone. It is easy enough that they can drift into being pleasant flatmates.
Sun|Uranus.friction: Sudden changes from one keep unsettling the other — plans altered, positions reversed, nothing of it malicious. The same argument recurs about reliability against room to move. Advance notice, even a short one, does most of the work.
Sun|Uranus.facing: A strong pull between wanting to be known and wanting to stay unpredictable. One offers solid ground, the other offers escape, and both are tempting. The gap only closes when freedom is granted openly rather than taken quietly.

Neptune|Sun.fused: One person's imagination attaches directly to who the other is, so being idealised is part of the deal from the first week. It is tender and genuinely inspiring. It is also hard to correct, because being seen accurately can feel like a demotion.
Neptune|Sun.easy: One softens the other's edges; the other gives the daydreaming something solid to attach to. Kindness comes easily here, and so does forgiveness. Keep an eye on excuses becoming automatic.
Neptune|Sun.friction: The picture one holds keeps failing to match the person in front of them, and the mismatch stings even though nobody lied. It resurfaces as a vague disappointment neither can name. It gets better when specific, unglamorous facts are said out loud.
Neptune|Sun.facing: A powerful pull, because each supplies what the other lacks — definition on one side, mystery on the other. The gap is that one wants to be seen clearly and the other prefers the version in their head. It survives on plain, unromantic questions about what is actually true.

Pluto|Sun.fused: What one will not let go of is wrapped around who the other is, which makes the bond intense and hard to walk away from. The loyalty is real and so is the pressure. Neither should let secrecy become the normal setting.
Pluto|Sun.easy: One person's depth gives the other somewhere to take the hard conversations, and those conversations do not end in collapse. Trust builds quickly. The ease can tip into intensity for its own sake — depth where a light evening would do.
Pluto|Sun.friction: One keeps pressing on something the other regards as strictly their own business, and the more it is guarded the harder it is pressed. It recurs as control dressed up as concern. Agreeing in advance what is genuinely private defuses most of it.
Pluto|Sun.facing: Magnetic and heavy at once: each senses the other could change them, which is both the attraction and the threat. Power gets quietly counted here — who gave in, who knows more. It only works while neither uses what they know as leverage.

Rahu|Sun.fused: The appetite for the untried sits right on the sense of self, so both keep pushing into territory neither has been in before. Exciting, and hungry — enough is a difficult word for this pair. Something ordinary has to be protected on purpose.
Rahu|Sun.easy: One person's pull towards the new flatters and enlarges the other, and neither has to argue for a change of direction. They grow fast together. The risk is momentum without a destination.
Rahu|Sun.friction: One person's restlessness keeps knocking the other off balance — a fresh obsession every few months, none of them finished. It comes back as a row about being serious. Finishing one thing together, however small, does more than any promise.
Rahu|Sun.facing: Real pull: one is settled in who they are, the other is chasing who they are not yet. Each looks like the answer to the other's problem, which is flattering and slightly unreal. Watch for one of them quietly becoming the other's project.

Ketu|Sun.fused: What one is quietly finished with is the very thing the other is built on, and it usually goes unspoken. There is often an odd familiarity, as though this has been done before. The work is stopping one person's detachment from reading as indifference to the other.
Ketu|Sun.easy: One person's willingness to let things go takes weight off the other — less needs defending, pride relaxes. It is calm and unforced. It can also drift, because neither supplies much push.
Ketu|Sun.friction: One keeps stepping back from exactly the thing the other needs to matter. It shows up as effort meeting a shrug. It improves when the detached one names plainly what they do still care about, instead of leaving it to be guessed.
Ketu|Sun.facing: One reaches for recognition, the other is already walking away from it, and each is quietly fascinated by the other's position. There is real pull, and a real gap about how much any of this should matter. It goes wrong if withdrawing becomes the standard move in a disagreement.

Moon|Moon.fused: Both of them are comforted by the same things, so home runs itself — same rhythms, same food, same idea of a good evening. Moods synchronise, which is warm on good days and airless on bad ones. When both dip at once, there is nobody left to steady the room.
Moon|Moon.easy: Their comforts differ without clashing, so each can settle down without the other having to change anything. Small kindnesses are guessed correctly most of the time. The ease can turn invisible — worth thanking each other for things that never had to be asked for.
Moon|Moon.friction: What settles one unsettles the other, usually over small household things: noise, tidiness, how much company counts as enough. It comes back weekly rather than yearly. Sorting out the practical arrangement works better than trying to talk each other out of a preference.
Moon|Moon.facing: Their needs sit at opposite ends — one soothed by closeness, the other by space — and each is drawn to what they do not have. Genuine warmth, genuine tug of war, usually over evenings and weekends. It works once both stop reading the other's need as a rejection.

Mercury|Moon.fused: Talking is how comfort happens for this pair: being heard and feeling safe are one and the same event. Conversation runs late and runs easily. The catch is that everything gets discussed, including things that would have settled on their own.
Mercury|Moon.easy: One person's way of explaining calms the other without effort — words land as reassurance rather than analysis. Difficult topics stay approachable. Because it is easy, they can talk around a hard feeling instead of through it.
Mercury|Moon.friction: One wants to work the problem, the other wants to feel steady first, and the timing is always slightly off. It recurs at the same moments: bad news, tiredness, late at night. Asking "do you want a solution or company?" heads off most of it.
Mercury|Moon.facing: One reasons out loud, the other reads the room, and each finds the other's method attractive and maddening in equal measure. The pull is real; so is the gap between what was said and what was felt. It works when the talkative one slows down and the quiet one says the thing rather than waiting for it to be noticed.

Moon|Venus.fused: The reassurance one of you needs and the warmth the other gives land in the same place, so affection arrives in exactly the shape it was wanted. That feels uncanny early on, and it also doubles up: when one is unsettled, the answer is more sweetness, so the hard conversation keeps getting postponed with a nice evening. Worth noticing when kindness is standing in for something that needs saying.
Moon|Venus.easy: Warmth here arrives in a form that actually lands — a made bed, a message at the right hour, a hand on the back — and neither of you has to explain what it meant. Comfort and affection agree without being negotiated. The catch is that it becomes wallpaper: because it never fails, it stops being noticed or thanked.
Moon|Venus.friction: The affection on offer and the comfort being asked for keep missing by a small margin — a gift when what was wanted was quiet company, a night out when what was wanted was an early night. Nobody is withholding anything, which makes it more irritating than a refusal, because it looks like it should have worked. It shifts quickly once each of you says, in plain specifics, what actually settles you.
Moon|Venus.facing: There is a real pull here: the way one shows warmth is appealing precisely because it is not how the other would do it. Across that same gap, the comfort one needs can read as demanding, and the warmth the other offers can read as performance. It works when neither treats their own version as the normal one.

Mars|Moon.fused: Feeling safe and going after things sit on the same spot, so restlessness comes out as push, and a disagreement lands directly where the comfort lives. Rows start fast and get personal quickly, and they can clear just as fast. The useful habit is saying which one is happening — 'I want to win this' or 'I want to be reassured'.
Mars|Moon.easy: Heat moves through this pair without damaging the ground underneath. One of you can be blunt, push hard, or lose their temper about the parking, and the other does not read it as care being withdrawn. The risk is never practising a real rupture, so the first serious one finds you both without any technique.
Mars|Moon.friction: The pace and volume of one person's pursuit keeps disturbing what the other needs to feel steady — decisions made quickly, a raised voice, plans announced rather than discussed. The row that keeps returning is about tone, not about the actual question. A warning — 'I'm going to push on this' — costs nothing and defuses most of it.
Mars|Moon.facing: One of you is settled by calm, the other by movement, and each finds the other's setting magnetic and tiring in equal measure. The pull is genuine: the restless one gets somewhere to land, the steady one gets moved. It goes wrong when 'calm down' and 'do something' become the only two things either of you says.

Jupiter|Moon.fused: Comfort and confidence sit together, so reassurance here comes as 'it'll be fine' — generously, at scale, and often. It is warm and it inflates: problems get talked into being solved before anything is done, and you both spend more on comfort than you meant to. Good weather, this — just keep an actual budget.
Jupiter|Moon.easy: The belief that things will work out genuinely steadies the other person here, not as a platitude but as something they can lean on. Plans feel possible, and a setback does not turn into a referendum on the relationship. Taken for granted, it means neither of you ever does the pessimistic version of the sums.
Jupiter|Moon.friction: The hopefulness keeps arriving too early. One of you offers 'it'll be fine' as help, the other hears their worry being waved away, and the worry gets louder in order to be taken seriously. The repair is small: hear the whole thing out first, then be encouraging.
Jupiter|Moon.facing: One of you feels safe with the known and the near; the other keeps opening windows. The attraction is real — one gets a horizon, the other gets a floor — and the failure is a stalemate where one is permanently the brake and the other permanently the engine. Swapping roles occasionally, on something small, breaks the pattern faster than arguing about it.

Moon|Saturn.fused: What one of you needs to feel safe is the same as what the other takes seriously, so care shows up as responsibility: bills paid, arrangements kept, weight carried without complaint. It is solid and it is heavy, and the cold snap, when it comes, lands exactly where the comfort was. Say the warm thing out loud sometimes; the structure will not say it for you.
Moon|Saturn.easy: Seriousness steadies rather than chills here. Turning up on time, remembering the appointment, doing what was said — these are meant as affection and received that way, with no translation needed. The thing to watch is that the practical quietly becomes the only register you speak in.
Moon|Saturn.friction: The instinct to go quiet and set terms arrives at the exact moment reassurance was wanted, and the silence gets read as punishment. It repeats because both of you are technically behaving well: one is being careful, one is asking to be met. Naming the withdrawal as it starts — 'I've gone quiet, it isn't about you' — takes most of the sting out.
Moon|Saturn.facing: One of you wants to be held; the other wants to make things safe by getting the arrangements right. The steadiness is genuinely attractive from one side and the softness genuinely attractive from the other. The gap sounds like 'you're cold' against 'I'm doing all of this for you', and both are true statements about different things.

Moon|Uranus.fused: Needing to feel safe and needing room sit on the same spot, so this pair is soothed by change and unsettled by too much routine. A last-minute plan feels like home; a standing Sunday obligation feels like a threat. It works while it is mutual, and it leaves you very little to fall back on in a bad month.
Moon|Uranus.easy: Space costs nothing here. One of you can disappear into work or a trip for days and the other does not read it as distance, and neither has to ask permission. What gets neglected is shared routine — with nothing forcing it, you can end up with plenty of freedom and not much shape.
Moon|Uranus.friction: Every time one of you takes room, the other's ground moves — and the trouble is almost never the going, it is the not saying when you are back. The same conversation returns because independence is being defended when what was asked for was information. A rough time of return, honoured, settles more of this than any talk about needs.
Moon|Uranus.facing: One of you wants to be reachable and known; the other wants the door left unlocked. Each finds the other's setting attractive — steadiness looks like rest, independence looks like air — and each can make the other feel accused. The pull holds as long as neither mistakes their own default for maturity.

Moon|Neptune.fused: Comfort and imagination land together, so being soothed and being enchanted are hard to tell apart. It is tender, and it blurs: what is actually happening and what is hoped for end up filed in the same drawer, sometimes for years. Anything factual — money, dates, what was actually agreed — is worth writing down.
Moon|Neptune.easy: Drifting together rests both of you: a film, a long aimless afternoon, a plan that may never happen. The imagining is restorative rather than escapist, and neither has to justify it to the other. The cost of it being so pleasant is that nobody checks the facts while the mood is good.
Moon|Neptune.friction: The picture one of you holds keeps not matching the person in front of them, and the mismatch surfaces as vagueness at exactly the moment a plain answer would have settled things. Disappointment turns up on a schedule, and it is usually about a promise nobody quite made. Asking for specifics early feels unromantic and prevents the slow version.
Moon|Neptune.facing: One of you wants what is real and countable; the other wants what is beautiful and possible. That is the attraction — each supplies what the other has not got — and it is also the accusation, 'you never dream' against 'you never look at what is actually here'. It works better when the dreaming and the accounting get separate evenings.

Moon|Pluto.fused: What one needs to feel safe and what the other will not release sit on the same spot, so attachment here is total and comfort has an undertow. Nothing is casual: a small withdrawal reads as abandonment, and a small return reads as everything being fine again. The intensity is real, and it is not, by itself, closeness.
Moon|Pluto.easy: Depth does not frighten either of you. You can go into money, jealousy, family or the past and come out closer rather than bruised, and neither treats a heavy conversation as an emergency. Because it is easy you may not realise how unusual it is, or how much warning other people need.
Moon|Pluto.friction: What one refuses to let go of presses exactly where the other needs ease — an old grievance re-entered, a rule that will not be renegotiated, a check that keeps being made. It returns because it is offered as care and received as control. It improves when the holding on is named as fear rather than defended as principle.
Moon|Pluto.facing: Being seen this thoroughly is both what one of you wanted and rather more than they asked for. The pull is strong, and so is the urge to retreat once the other has got that close. It stays workable while both accept that not everything has to be excavated to be loved.

Moon|Rahu.fused: The appetite for the untried sits right on top of the need for safety, so hunger and homesickness get confused: when what was needed was rest, this pair books something. It makes for a life with a great deal in it. It also means the settling never quite happens unless you put it in the diary on purpose.
Moon|Rahu.easy: New things do not destabilise you. A change of city, job or plan can happen and the base holds, because neither of you reads novelty as a threat to the two of you. The habit worth keeping is checking that the moving is still wanted rather than simply assumed.
Moon|Rahu.friction: One of you keeps reaching for the next thing before the last one was discussed, and the other keeps having their footing moved. The recurring row is not about the adventure itself but about being told rather than asked. Agreeing what counts as a decision, and what is only an idea said out loud, takes most of it away.
Moon|Rahu.facing: One holds the known ground, the other wants what has not been tried, and each is exactly what the other has not got. That is the attraction and it is also the insult — stuck against reckless, usually said in those words within the same fortnight. It holds when the anchor gets thanked as often as the explorer does.

Ketu|Moon.fused: The place one of you goes for comfort is the same place the other has quietly finished with, so warmth here tends to arrive with a shrug. There is real ease in that — little clinging, quick forgiveness — and a strange thinness, where things get dropped that were worth keeping. Notice what you are both letting go of by default rather than by choice.
Ketu|Moon.easy: Neither of you holds a grudge for long, and things that would sit heavily elsewhere get put down here without ceremony. Ordinary trouble is cheap to survive between you. The flip side is that endings are cheap too, and something can be released before anyone has really argued for keeping it.
Ketu|Moon.friction: One keeps letting go of what the other is still using for comfort — a flat, a tradition, a friendship, a Sunday habit. The hurt that returns is 'why do you not care about this', and the honest answer is usually that they genuinely no longer do. It becomes workable once keeping a thing is asked for directly instead of assumed to be shared.
Ketu|Moon.facing: One of you wants to be held; the other has already taken a step back and is not sure why that is a problem. The unbotheredness is restful and maddening by turns, and it is a large part of the attraction. The gap closes when detachment stops being treated as wisdom and needing someone stops being treated as weakness.

Mercury|Mercury.fused: Both of you think and talk at the same pace and by the same route, so half a sentence is enough and a joke needs no set-up. The shorthand is a genuine pleasure, and it means there is nobody in the room to say 'you have lost me'. Your blind spots are identical, so a bad idea can travel a long way here without being stopped.
Mercury|Mercury.easy: Talking is cheap between you in the best sense — a conversation can be picked up days later, mid-thought, without either of you resenting the effort. Neither has to translate for the other. Because it flows so well, you can talk constantly and still not have said the thing that matters, so it is worth asking now and then what has not come up.
Mercury|Mercury.friction: You process at different speeds and by different routes: one thinks out loud, the other needs to sit with it, and each keeps reading the other's method as not taking it seriously. The misunderstanding is nearly always about format rather than content. Saying which mode you are in — 'this is me thinking, not me deciding' — removes most of it.
Mercury|Mercury.facing: One of you goes straight to the detail, the other to the shape of the whole thing; one wants it written, the other wants it said. It is genuinely useful, since between you very little gets missed, and genuinely irritating, since each is convinced the other is taking the long way round. Handing over the part you are worse at works better than trying to meet in the middle.

Mercury|Venus.fused: Talking and showing affection are the same act here: the warmth arrives as words, and it arrives often. It is charming, and it makes silence expensive — a quiet week can feel like love withdrawn when it is only a busy week. Worth agreeing what still counts as affection when neither of you has the energy to be delightful.
Mercury|Venus.easy: Being funny lands as being kind here. Teasing does not wound, compliments get believed rather than deflected, and the ordinary business of the week is pleasant to conduct. The thing to watch is that charm covers a lot of ground, including ground that needed doing rather than discussing.
Mercury|Venus.friction: The teasing one means fondly keeps landing as criticism, or the careful wording meant as tact reads as cool. It recurs because both of you are being pleasant on purpose and neither can see why it is not working. Asking what a line meant, instead of reacting to how it sounded, is the whole repair.
Mercury|Venus.facing: One of you shows care by talking it through; the other by quietly doing something and saying nothing about it. Each finds the other's way admirable and not quite enough — 'you never say it' against 'I show you constantly' — and both are describing the same affection. It lasts longer if you learn to read the other's currency rather than asking them to change it.

Mars|Mercury.fused: Thinking and going after things are one motion here, so ideas arrive already sharpened and arguing is how the thinking gets done. It is quick and often brilliant. It also means one of you can be in a contest the other did not know had started, so say when you are only testing an idea.
Mars|Mercury.easy: Bluntness does no damage here. You can interrupt, disagree flatly and decide fast, and none of it costs anything between you. Remember that the same sharpness, aimed at someone outside the pair, does land as rudeness — you have simply stopped noticing it.
Mars|Mercury.friction: One person's argument keeps outrunning the other's thinking, so the conversation quietly turns into a contest with a winner. The pattern is winning the point and losing the evening, again and again, usually over something neither of you cares about by morning. Separating 'we are deciding' from 'we are talking' clears most of it.
Mars|Mercury.facing: One of you wants it settled now; the other wants it turned over first, and each finds the other's mode compelling and exhausting. The pull is that between you a decision gets both examined and actually made. It sours when speed is called stupidity and care is called stalling.

Jupiter|Mercury.fused: Thinking and expecting it to work out sit together, so ideas here arrive large, confident and fluent. You will talk each other into things, and the detail is the usual casualty — the plan is excellent right up to the bit nobody costed. Write the boring part down while the enthusiasm is still on.
Jupiter|Mercury.easy: The optimism gives the thinking room: an idea gets encouraged before it gets corrected, so far more of them survive being said out loud. That is rarer and more valuable than it sounds. The cost is that very little gets tested, so the one dud is expensive when it comes.
Jupiter|Mercury.friction: One of you keeps offering a detail and having it waved through as a technicality; the other keeps offering enthusiasm and getting a caveat. The recurring argument is about scale — whether this is a big plan or a small one — dressed up as an argument about facts. Settling the size first makes the rest of the conversation possible.
Jupiter|Mercury.facing: One is precise, the other expansive, and each is the reason the other is credible: the vision needs the numbers, and the numbers need a reason to exist. The gap sounds like pedantry against waffle, and you have both said it. It works when the precise one is asked for the risk rather than for the objection.

Mercury|Saturn.fused: Thinking and taking things seriously land together, so words carry weight here — nothing is said lightly and nothing is heard lightly either. It makes for careful, honest conversation, and it crowds out play: a passing remark gets treated as a stated position. Say when you are only musing.
Mercury|Saturn.easy: The seriousness makes the thinking useful: plans get written down, decisions get remembered, and neither of you has to chase the other for what was agreed. You are quietly excellent at logistics. Left alone, logistics becomes the only thing you talk about.
Mercury|Saturn.friction: Every idea meets an objection before it is finished, and eventually the other person stops offering — which is worse for both of you than the bad ideas ever were. It repeats because half-formed thoughts keep being received as proposals. Labelling them as they leave your mouth is enough to change it.
Mercury|Saturn.facing: One thinks by talking wide and fast, the other by narrowing and cutting, and between you something appears that neither could manage alone. The gap shows up as one feeling edited and the other feeling flooded. It holds if the cutting comes after the flow rather than during it.

Mercury|Uranus.fused: The talking and the need for room land on the same spot, so conversation itself becomes the escape hatch. Ideas arrive fast, get said fast, and change fast — thrilling, and it means a plan made on Tuesday may not survive Thursday. Nothing feels more confining here than being asked to repeat yesterday's opinion.
Mercury|Uranus.easy: One of you talks things out; the other needs room to move, and the talk naturally leaves that room. Questions come without a summons attached, so neither of you feels pinned by a conversation. The risk is assuming it will always be this effortless and never actually saying how much space you need.
Mercury|Uranus.friction: One of you wants to finish the sentence; the other has already got up from the table. It shows up as half-conversations, plans revised mid-flight, and a recurring complaint that one never explains and the other never stops explaining. Naming it as a difference in pace, not in care, is usually what settles it.
Mercury|Uranus.facing: One of you thinks by talking it through; the other thinks by getting away from everyone and doing something odd. The pull is real — that unpredictability is genuinely interesting to talk to — and so is the gap, because a conversation that runs long starts to feel like a cage. It works best when the talking has a clear end.

Mercury|Neptune.fused: Words and daydreams come from the same place here, so what gets described is often better than what exists. Conversations are atmospheric and moving, and the details are slippery a week later. Lovely for stories and plans; hard for who is picking up the shopping.
Mercury|Neptune.easy: One of you puts things into words; the other supplies the pictures, and the two fit without anybody working at it. Vague feelings get named gently rather than interrogated. Because it is easy, neither of you may notice how rarely anything gets pinned to a date.
Mercury|Neptune.friction: One of you asks what exactly was meant; the other genuinely cannot say, because it was a feeling and not a sentence. The snag repeats: precise questions land as pressure, soft answers land as evasion. It eases once you agree which things get written down and which are allowed to stay blurry.
Mercury|Neptune.facing: One of you wants it clear, the other wants it beautiful, and each is drawn to what the other has. There is real attraction in being understood without being cross-examined, and real tension when a plain question meets an answer made of mist. That gap is worth crossing on purpose rather than assuming.

Mercury|Pluto.fused: Talking here goes straight to the bottom of things, and small talk does not survive long. The same intensity means an offhand remark can be turned over for days and quoted back months later. Honest and searching at its best; interrogative and hard to leave at its worst.
Mercury|Pluto.easy: One of you says the difficult thing plainly; the other can hear it without flinching. Serious subjects get raised at ordinary times, which most pairs never manage. The ease can hide how much weight the quieter one is carrying — being able to discuss something is not the same as having put it down.
Mercury|Pluto.friction: One of you wants to talk it through now; the other goes silent and keeps the file open. Words said in a rush get stored rather than dropped, and come back later with a date attached. Progress comes from agreeing out loud what counts as finished, instead of assuming a conversation ended because it stopped.
Mercury|Pluto.facing: One of you keeps things moving and light; the other holds on to what mattered and will not be jollied out of it. That steadiness is magnetic, and exhausting when a passing comment gets treated as evidence. Real pull across a real gap: neither of you should have to become the other.

Mercury|Rahu.fused: Curiosity and conversation feed each other here, so the newest idea always sounds like the true one. Excellent for spotting things early, risky for finishing them, because the next thing arrives before the last is done. Expect a lot of started projects and a lot of good instincts.
Mercury|Rahu.easy: One of you likes talking things over; the other is always heading somewhere untested, and the talk keeps up without strain. Novelty gets examined instead of only chased. Because it flows, you may never build the habit of asking whether an exciting idea is also a good one.
Mercury|Rahu.friction: One of you wants the plan explained; the other wants to try it and see. Explanations feel like brakes, questions feel like doubt, and the same argument returns with a different subject each time. It settles when one agrees to run the small version and the other stops asking for certainty first.
Mercury|Rahu.facing: One of you sorts things and puts them into words; the other is pulled towards whatever has not been done yet. The attraction is that each makes the other bigger — sharper thinking on one side, braver moves on the other. The tension is that care can look like cowardice from one side and recklessness from the other.

Ketu|Mercury.fused: Words and letting go sit in the same place, so things get said once and then quietly dropped. Conversation can be unusually clean, with no scorekeeping, and also strangely absent, with topics abandoned halfway. Silence here is more often peace than sulking, which is worth knowing about each other.
Ketu|Mercury.easy: One of you talks; the other does not need the last word or a full account. Disagreements deflate rather than escalate. The ease is genuine, though it can slide into never quite finishing the things that mattered.
Ketu|Mercury.friction: One of you needs to talk it out; the other has already stopped caring about the subject and cannot fake interest. That reads as dismissal, and it returns whenever something feels unresolved to one and finished to the other. "I need you to stay in this for ten more minutes" does more work here than any argument.
Ketu|Mercury.facing: One of you gathers detail and wants it understood; the other is busy putting things down. There is real relief in the company of someone who does not hoard grievances, and real frustration when a careful explanation meets a shrug. The gap closes when stepping back is announced rather than just performed.

Venus|Venus.fused: You both express warmth in the same currency — the same gestures, the same timing, the same idea of what counts as thoughtful. Being understood without translation is rare and very comfortable. The catch is a shared blind spot: whatever neither of you thinks to offer, nobody offers.
Venus|Venus.easy: You both give affection in ways the other recognises straight away, so kindness needs no decoding. Tastes overlap enough that choosing a meal, a room or a gift is not a negotiation. It is so comfortable that you may stop asking what the other actually wants.
Venus|Venus.friction: You both mean well and keep missing. One shows care by doing something practical, the other by giving time and attention, and each keeps offering their own version harder. It stops being a snag when you swap lists instead of increasing effort.
Venus|Venus.facing: You both want closeness and go about it in opposite ways — one moves in, the other waits to be chosen. The attraction is obvious and so is the standoff, since each is waiting for the gesture they would make themselves. Deciding who reaches first, this time, beats waiting patiently.

Mars|Venus.fused: Wanting and pursuing sit in the same place, so affection and conflict run down one wire. Arguments can turn warm and warmth can turn into a contest, sometimes within the same hour. Heat is not the problem here; knowing when to stop is.
Mars|Venus.easy: One of you shows warmth; the other goes after what they want, and the two rarely misread each other. Being pursued feels like being appreciated, and disagreements do not cost much. It is easy enough that neither of you finds out what happens when it is not — worth testing before it matters.
Mars|Venus.friction: One of you wants tenderness; the other wants it settled now. Affection gets offered at the wrong moment and read as avoidance, or a sharp remark gets read as love being withdrawn. The recurring fix is timing: argue or comfort, but not both at once.
Mars|Venus.facing: One of you softens things and the other sharpens them, and each finds the other's approach unreasonable and attractive at the same time. This is the pair that makes up as vividly as it falls out. The gap is that one needs the argument finished and the other needs it never to have started.

Jupiter|Venus.fused: Warmth and hopefulness land together, so generosity here is easy and large. It feels wonderful and it overshoots — promises, spending, plans made in a good mood that must be honoured in a flat one. Almost nobody in this pattern is stingy; scale is the thing to watch.
Jupiter|Venus.easy: One of you gives affection freely; the other assumes it will all be fine, and that assumption makes the giving safe. Small hurts do not harden, because neither of you expects the worst. The risk of ease is complacency — being hopeful is not the same as paying attention.
Jupiter|Venus.friction: One of you wants a specific gesture; the other offers reassurance that everything is fine. Optimism starts to feel like not being taken seriously, and the same disappointment comes back in different clothes. It helps when the hopeful one hears the complaint out before solving it.
Jupiter|Venus.facing: One of you loves in the particular — this person, this evening; the other trusts broadly that things work out. There is real warmth across that gap and real irritation, because faith in the future can look like inattention to the present. Both are useful; neither should be asked to convert.

Saturn|Venus.fused: Affection and seriousness occupy the same ground, so love here is treated as a commitment rather than a mood. That makes it slow and durable. The same setting can flip: when things go wrong, warmth does not get loud, it goes quiet and cold.
Saturn|Venus.easy: One of you offers warmth; the other keeps their word, and the two hold each other up without effort. Affection is shown by turning up, repeatedly, over years. Reliability is the easiest thing in the world to take for granted — say thank you for it out loud sometimes.
Saturn|Venus.friction: One of you wants closeness now; the other wants to know it is earned and safe first. Warmth meets a raised eyebrow, and the snag repeats: one feels rationed, the other feels rushed. It improves when the cautious one names the fear instead of simply going quiet.
Saturn|Venus.facing: One of you leads with warmth, the other with standards, and each is drawn to what they lack. The pull is genuine — being taken seriously is a kind of love, and so is being delighted in. The tension is that one hears "not yet" as "not really", and the other hears eagerness as unseriousness.

Uranus|Venus.fused: Warmth and the need for room sit on the same spot, so affection arrives in bursts and dislikes being scheduled. Spontaneous kindness is plentiful; routine tenderness is not. It is exciting, and ordinary reassurance is harder to come by than either of you expects.
Uranus|Venus.easy: One of you shows affection; the other needs space, and the affection is offered in a way that fences nobody in. Freedom and closeness are not treated as rivals here. Because it is easy, you may never have actually agreed what you owe each other.
Uranus|Venus.friction: One of you wants a rhythm — the same evening, the same warmth; the other bolts as soon as anything hardens into an expectation. It shows up as small broken plans, each minor and each adding up. It eases when the loose one commits to a little, precisely, rather than a lot, vaguely.
Uranus|Venus.facing: One of you wants to be close; the other wants to be free, and the wanting runs both ways. The attraction is that each is exactly the thing the other keeps at arm's length. It works when space is granted before it is grabbed, and closeness is asked for rather than tested.

Neptune|Venus.fused: Love and imagination sit together, so affection is tender, atmospheric and often aimed slightly past the actual person. At its best it is unusually gentle. It is also where disappointment comes from comparing someone with your own picture of them.
Neptune|Venus.easy: One of you shows warmth; the other sees the best version, and the effect is forgiving without anyone trying. Small failings genuinely do not matter much here. Take care that forgiving does not quietly become not noticing.
Neptune|Venus.friction: One of you wants affection that shows up in ordinary ways; the other keeps offering something more dreamlike. Promises are meant sincerely and kept unevenly, and the same hurt recurs — not out of coldness but out of vagueness. Small, concrete, dated commitments do more for this pair than any grand declaration.
Neptune|Venus.facing: One of you loves the person in front of them; the other loves an ideal, and both feel the pull across that distance. It can be enchanting, and it can leave one of you feeling adored but not actually seen. "What am I like when I'm not at my best?" is a useful question to ask out loud.

Pluto|Venus.fused: Affection and holding on occupy the same ground, so love here is never casual — it goes all the way down or not at all. That is intense and genuinely loyal. It also brings jealousy, and old hurts that never quite file themselves away.
Pluto|Venus.easy: One of you gives warmth; the other holds on, and the holding feels like devotion rather than a grip. Depth arrives quickly and frightens neither of you. The ease can hide how much is being kept — depth without a habit of airing things gets heavy slowly.
Pluto|Venus.friction: One of you wants affection to be light sometimes; the other cannot be light about anything that matters. Reassurance gets asked for again and again and never quite lands, and the same test returns in new forms. It settles when the intense one says the fear plainly instead of arranging a situation that proves it.
Pluto|Venus.facing: One of you offers warmth openly; the other keeps a firm hold on what they value, and the pull between them is strong enough to be uncomfortable. Being wanted that much is flattering and heavy at once. The gap holds as long as the openness is not punished and the holding is not hidden.

Rahu|Venus.fused: Warmth and the appetite for the untried sit together, so attraction here is fast, strong and drawn to the unfamiliar. It makes for a vivid beginning. The same pull keeps looking outwards, so what is already yours can quietly stop counting.
Rahu|Venus.easy: One of you gives affection; the other keeps reaching for something new, and the two feed each other instead of competing. Boredom gets no foothold. Even so, someone has to notice when novelty is standing in for closeness.
Rahu|Venus.friction: One of you wants to be chosen again; the other is already interested in the next thing. Enthusiasm arrives and drains on its own schedule, leaving the warmer one checking the temperature. It improves when the restless one aims that appetite inward — new things done together, not instead.
Rahu|Venus.facing: One of you offers steady warmth; the other is pulled hard towards whatever has not been tried. Across that gap the attraction is real and a little dazzling, and so is the worry that you are being enjoyed as an experience. Being honest about the appetite works better than pretending it is not there.

Ketu|Venus.fused: Affection and letting go land in the same place, so love here is offered without much grasping. It can be unusually generous and free of scorekeeping. It can also feel like a door left open — warmth that asks for nothing can read as warmth that does not need you.
Ketu|Venus.easy: One of you shows warmth; the other holds it lightly, so nothing turns possessive. Small slights simply fall away. The ease has a price: what you both stop mentioning can end up never being mentioned at all.
Ketu|Venus.friction: One of you wants affection returned in kind; the other has quietly stepped back and cannot manufacture the feeling on demand. The reaching one tries harder, the detached one withdraws further, and round it goes. Naming the withdrawal without accusing anyone is what breaks the loop.
Ketu|Venus.facing: One of you moves towards, the other is already loosening their hold, and the space between them is oddly compelling. There is a calm here that is genuinely restful and a distance that is genuinely lonely. It works when the one letting go says what they still want, instead of leaving it to be guessed.

Mars|Mars.fused: Both of them go after what they want at the same speed and in the same way, and both reach the shouting point at the same moment. Nothing needs explaining here, which is a relief — but there is no cool head left in the room when one is needed. Rows tend to be short and loud, and they either clear the air quickly or come back the following week unchanged.
Mars|Mars.easy: Both of them push hard, but not at the same things, so effort rarely turns into competition for the same ground. Plans get started without a negotiation about who leads, and a disagreement usually stays a disagreement rather than becoming a fight. The thing that goes unnoticed is that neither ever makes the other do the difficult thing they have been avoiding.
Mars|Mars.friction: Both want to move first, but not at the same tempo, so the same argument about pace keeps returning in new clothes. One reads the other's urgency as bullying; the other reads the delay as a refusal dressed up as caution. Naming who starts things and who finishes them takes most of the heat out of it.
Mars|Mars.facing: Each one's push meets the other's head-on, and the irritation and the attraction come from exactly the same place. Competition is real between them, and it can be sporting or corrosive depending on whether they can get onto the same side. Point them at one shared problem — a deadline, a move, a leaking roof — and the friction turns into fuel.

Jupiter|Mars.fused: The urge to act and the belief that it will all work out land on the same spot, so plans get big fast and start the same afternoon. It is genuinely energising, and it also means nobody in the room is quietly doing the sums. Decide early who is allowed to call something too big, because otherwise no one will.
Jupiter|Mars.easy: The one who moves finds someone who says yes; the one who says yes finds someone who actually goes and does it. Confidence turns into motion here with very little effort, which is why it gets taken for granted. Over time it can drift into overreach — the encouragement never runs out, so the brakes never get tested.
Jupiter|Mars.friction: One wants to start now, the other wants to keep the options open a little longer, and each reads the other as reckless or as dithering. The encouragement tends to arrive just after the moment for it has passed, or the push arrives before the idea was worth pushing. Fixing a size and a date together, before anyone gets excited, settles most of it.
Jupiter|Mars.facing: There is a real pull across this gap: the driven one is drawn to that easy faith, and the hopeful one is drawn to someone who actually moves. The same pull can make them worse together — a plan grows to the size of one person's confidence and the other's willingness to charge at it. The useful correction is an outside opinion, not a smaller dream.

Mars|Saturn.fused: The push and the caution sit right on top of each other, so effort here is disciplined and very little of it is wasted. It can also mean the accelerator and the handbrake are pressed at the same time: a lot of strain, not much movement. Watch the one who goes quiet rather than argues — that silence is where the real disagreement is.
Mars|Saturn.easy: One person's drive gets shape from the other's seriousness, and difficult, boring jobs actually get finished. Neither has to argue for patience or for effort; both are simply assumed. The cost of an arrangement this smooth is that it stops being noticed — say out loud what the other one is carrying.
Mars|Saturn.friction: The eager one experiences the careful one as a brake; the careful one experiences the eager one as noise. It plays out identically each time: a plan, a hesitation, a sharp remark, then a withdrawal that lasts longer than the row did. Because a cold reply lands harder than a hot one, the repair usually has to start from the quieter side.
Mars|Saturn.facing: Heat on one side and cold on the other, and each finds the other's setting oddly compelling. The pull is genuine — one wants to be steadied, the other wants to be moved — and so is the tension when steadying starts to look like refusal. It works far better with separate jobs and clear deadlines than with one of them supervising the other.

Mars|Uranus.fused: The urge to act and the need to be unconstrained fire together, so decisions get made suddenly and announced afterwards. Life between them is rarely dull and rarely planned. What needs protecting is anything that requires steady upkeep, because that is the first thing to be dropped.
Mars|Uranus.easy: One person's push does not threaten the other's independence — going off alone reads as ordinary here, not as rejection. Plans change without anyone taking offence, which spares them a great many arguments. Left unexamined for years, it can quietly become two busy people living in parallel and hardly noticing.
Mars|Uranus.friction: The chase keeps running into the need for room: one presses for an answer, the other needs to be somewhere else before giving one. From the outside it looks like a sudden refusal over nothing at all. Asking instead of pressing, and agreeing a time to come back to it, defuses most of these.
Mars|Uranus.facing: One pursues, one bolts, and neither can quite leave the pattern alone. Being wanted that plainly and being that hard to pin down are both genuinely attractive, and both exhausting after the third year of it. It settles when the freedom is offered before it has to be demanded.

Mars|Neptune.fused: The push and the daydream occupy the same place, so effort goes where the longing is rather than where the plan is. Wonderful for anything creative; unreliable for anything with a date attached. Be careful what gets idealised between them, because it will then be chased very hard.
Mars|Neptune.easy: The one who acts gives the other's imagining somewhere to land, and the dreaming takes the edge off the pushing. Disagreements dissolve easily here — sometimes too easily, because a real complaint can be turned into a mood and then quietly dropped. Write the annoying things down; those are the ones that go missing.
Mars|Neptune.friction: One asks a direct question and gets a mist; the other asks to be understood and gets a plan. The recurring snag is vagueness that reads as evasion, met with bluntness that reads as attack. Putting the specific request and the specific feeling in the same sentence stops the loop faster than any amount of patience.
Mars|Neptune.facing: A strong pull across a wide gap: the vivid one wants somebody who acts, the direct one wants somebody who sees more than the facts. What each finds enchanting is also what leaves them feeling unmet — the fog, the force. Be literal about arrangements and generous about meanings, and the distance stays interesting rather than lonely.

Mars|Pluto.fused: Effort and the refusal to let go sit on the same spot, so whatever these two take on is pursued to the end. It is formidable, and it is heavy to live inside. The same intensity that finishes things can turn a small argument into a matter of principle within about a minute.
Mars|Pluto.easy: The drive has somewhere deep to go, and the depth has someone willing to move it along. They can get through a genuinely hard year without either of them giving up. The risk of it working so well is that neither notices when they are still gripping something that stopped mattering a long time ago.
Mars|Pluto.friction: One pushes openly, the other holds on quietly, and pressure builds in a place nobody has named. It resurfaces as a fight about something small, months later, carrying far more force than the subject can explain. Saying the actual stake out loud early, even when it sounds too big for the occasion, is what breaks the cycle.
Mars|Pluto.facing: A charged pull: the direct one is drawn to what will not be shifted, and the immovable one to what will not back off. Power is the live question here — who yields, who insists, who is keeping count. Fought openly it can be honest and even bonding; fought through hints and silence it corrodes.

Mars|Rahu.fused: The push and the appetite for the untried land together, so this pair starts things constantly, usually before the last one was finished. Very fast, very alive, and poor at endings. Keep a short list of what has to be completed before anything new is allowed to begin.
Mars|Rahu.easy: A hunger for the unfamiliar meets someone happy to actually go, so trips, moves and new ventures happen rather than getting discussed. It flows so easily that nobody checks whether all this newness adds up to anything. One honest conversation a year about what they are building, rather than what they are doing, is worth more than it sounds.
Mars|Rahu.friction: The urge to chase and the urge to try something else keep arriving out of step — one commits just as the other loses interest. It reads as flakiness from one side and rigidity from the other, and both readings are unfair. Setting a firm end date for the current thing, before the next one appears, removes most of the argument.
Mars|Rahu.facing: Real pull: the driven one is fascinated by an appetite bigger than their own, and the restless one wants somebody who will actually give chase. It tips into excess easily, because neither is offering a reason to stop and both are enjoying not being offered one. Keep one dull shared commitment as ballast and the rest can be as fast as they like.

Ketu|Mars.fused: The push and the willingness to walk away land on the same spot, so effort here can end abruptly and without much explanation. It makes for clean exits and unfinished projects in roughly equal measure. There is a difference between a thing being finished and a person having gone cold on it, and from the inside those two feel identical.
Ketu|Mars.easy: One presses, the other genuinely does not need to win, so conflicts end early and nothing gets dragged out for days. That is a rare comfort. Over years it can become lopsided — one keeps deciding, the other keeps not minding, and neither notices when it stopped being a choice.
Ketu|Mars.friction: The pursuing one wants a response and gets detachment instead, which lands as indifference rather than the peace it was meant as. The snag repeats: pushing harder produces more distance, and the distance produces more pushing. Asking for a plain yes or no, rather than for a reaction, is what interrupts it.
Ketu|Mars.facing: A genuine pull across a real gap — one is stirred by someone so unbothered, the other by someone who still cares that much. The tension underneath is about how much anything ought to matter. It goes well when the letting go is agreed between them, and badly when it is a way of leaving the room without saying so.

Jupiter|Jupiter.fused: Both of them expect things to work out, about the same things, at the same moment. It is a warm and generous place to live, and guests notice it. It also means nobody in the household is worried, so the first bad news tends to arrive as a surprise to both at once.
Jupiter|Jupiter.easy: Both of them are hopeful, but about different things, so one can stay steady while the other is carried away. Encouragement is plentiful and costs nothing here. The unnoticed part is that neither of them ever says a flat no, so the small doubts never get said aloud until they are large ones.
Jupiter|Jupiter.friction: Both believe it will be fine, but on different terms — one trusts the plan, the other trusts the feeling, and each thinks the other's confidence is misplaced. It resurfaces whenever something calls for generosity: money, guests, second chances, lending things. Agreeing what generosity actually costs, in numbers, ends most of it.
Jupiter|Jupiter.facing: Two large appetites for possibility, pointed at each other across a real distance, each expanding in its own direction. The attraction is obvious; the tension is that neither wants to be the one who contracts to make room. Growth here needs a shared budget rather than a shared mood.

Jupiter|Saturn.fused: Hope and caution sit in the same place, so optimism here arrives with a cost estimate already attached. That combination is rarer and more useful than it sounds. It can also turn every good idea into a project plan before anybody has had the chance to enjoy it.
Jupiter|Saturn.easy: One person's confidence gets a floor under it and the other's seriousness gets some air. Between them they can promise things and then keep them, which is not common. Because it works so quietly, both may forget what the arrangement is doing — the cautious one is not cold, and the hopeful one is not naive.
Jupiter|Saturn.friction: One arrives with an idea, the other names the problem, and within a minute both feel unheard. Repeated for long enough, the hopeful one stops mentioning things and the careful one concludes that nothing was ever serious. Splitting it in two — enthusiasm today, objections tomorrow — is unglamorous and works.
Jupiter|Saturn.facing: A real pull between someone who adds possibilities and someone who subtracts them, each recognising something they lack in the other. Taking turns, it is genuinely stabilising; taking positions, it grinds. Watch for the moment either of them starts making the other's argument sarcastically — that is the sign it has become a habit rather than a conversation.

Jupiter|Uranus.fused: Faith that it will work out and the need for room fire together, so large changes get made cheerfully and quickly. Leaving jobs, moving country, starting over — none of that frightens this pair. The bill turns up later, and it is nearly always about the things that needed continuity.
Jupiter|Uranus.easy: One person's optimism makes the other's independence feel unthreatening, and the freedom keeps the optimism from going stale. Nobody has to justify wanting time alone or wanting something different. Left to itself it can drift, though: both keep saying yes to elsewhere, and very little accumulates between them.
Jupiter|Uranus.friction: The hopeful plan and the sudden change of direction keep colliding — one has just told everyone it is happening, the other has just decided otherwise. Each reads the other as unreliable or as inflexible, and each is a bit right. Booking fewer things further ahead, and meaning them, cuts the number of these arguments sharply.
Jupiter|Uranus.facing: A strong pull: one is drawn to a life that could still turn into anything, the other to somebody who makes the leap feel survivable. Across the gap, the real argument is whether a promise is a comfort or a cage. It works when both of them promise less and keep more.

Jupiter|Neptune.fused: Belief and longing occupy the same spot, and the result is a shared picture of the future that neither of them ever questions. It is beautiful, and it is very hard to check against anything. Somebody outside the pair will have to be the one who asks the plain questions.
Jupiter|Neptune.easy: Hope and imagination feed each other gently here — kindness comes easily, so does forgiveness, and the mood between them is generous. The blind spot is the same as the gift: things get given away, excused or believed with very little examined. Keep the money and the promises written down, and leave the rest exactly as it is.
Jupiter|Neptune.friction: One offers encouragement when the other wanted to be understood rather than cheered up. Or the vision keeps growing at precisely the moment the promise needed narrowing. The snag repeats around things agreed in a warm moment and remembered differently later, so write down what was actually decided, on the day.
Jupiter|Neptune.facing: A real pull across a real gap — one supplies the faith, the other supplies the vision, and each mistakes the other's for their own. Together they can talk themselves into almost anything, and be genuinely hurt when it does not hold up. Dream out loud and decide in writing, and this becomes one of the warmer pairings there is.

Jupiter|Pluto.fused: Optimism and the refusal to let go land together, so whatever this pair believes in gets pursued with unusual force. They can move things that other people have written off. They can also find a conviction almost impossible to revise once it has set.
Jupiter|Pluto.easy: Confidence gets some depth and the depth gets some daylight, so they can take on something serious without it souring. Hard subjects — money, illness, family — can actually be talked about here. Because it goes well, the stakes tend to rise without anyone deciding to raise them.
Jupiter|Pluto.friction: One wants to move on generously; the other is still holding what happened. The recurring snag is forgiveness — offered too early on one side, withheld too long on the other, with both certain they are the reasonable one. What helps is separating letting something go from pretending it never mattered.
Jupiter|Pluto.facing: A charged pull: one is drawn to intensity, the other to someone who is not frightened by it. The tension shows up as control dressed as encouragement, or suspicion dressed as realism. Name the actual stake — it is usually who decides — and the heat becomes useful rather than corrosive.

Jupiter|Rahu.fused: Faith that it will work out and appetite for the untried sit on the same spot, so this pair says yes fast and says it often. Doors open for them that stay shut for more cautious people. Nothing in this combination reduces the size of anything, so the limit has to be set deliberately or it will not exist.
Jupiter|Rahu.easy: The hunger for something new meets encouragement rather than resistance, and the encouragement gets somewhere to go. They will try the restaurant, take the job, book the flight, move the date forward. The unnoticed cost is that refusing never gets practised, so it is not available on the day it is needed.
Jupiter|Rahu.friction: The wish for more keeps outrunning the belief that it will be fine, or turns up just as the other has finally settled. It repeats around scale: one wants bigger, the other wanted better, and each hears the other as greedy or as timid. Deciding once, in plain numbers, what enough looks like buys a year of quiet.
Jupiter|Rahu.facing: A strong mutual pull, and a shared weakness for excess — each makes the other's appetite look perfectly reasonable. Across the gap, one wants meaning from the new thing while the other simply wants the new thing. Keep one person's veto real, and this is an adventurous pairing rather than a hectic one.

Jupiter|Ketu.fused: One person's faith that things will turn out lands right on top of the other's willingness to walk away, and each keeps feeding the other. You can be marvellously unbothered together — big plans held loosely, no panic when one falls through. The snag is that nobody in the room is arguing for finishing the thing.
Jupiter|Ketu.easy: The hopeful one makes room for the other's habit of dropping what has stopped working, without reading it as giving up. In turn, the letting-go steadies the optimism, so it stops attaching itself to every passing scheme. This runs so smoothly you may never notice it is doing anything.
Jupiter|Ketu.friction: The hopeful one keeps saying it is worth another go; the other has already quietly closed the door. It returns as a recurring argument about whether you are being realistic or defeatist, and both readings are partly right. It eases when the optimist names what specifically would change their mind, and the other says out loud when they have let go rather than just going silent.
Jupiter|Ketu.facing: Real pull here: the buoyant one finds the other's lack of clinging restful, and the detached one finds the other's belief warming. Across the gap, each also finds the other slightly maddening — one always adding, one always subtracting. Neither of you is the sensible one; you are the two halves of a decision.

Saturn|Saturn.fused: Both of them take the same things seriously and go cold in the same place. It makes for a formidable pair — the same standards, the same impatience with waffle, no need to explain why the rule matters. But when that shared cold spot gets touched, there is nobody left in the room who thinks it is a small thing.
Saturn|Saturn.easy: They take life seriously in ways that fit together rather than compete. One's discipline props up the other's without either having to argue for it, and the day-to-day rules more or less write themselves. Because it costs them nothing, they tend to underestimate how rare it is.
Saturn|Saturn.friction: Both are serious people, but about different things, and each reads the other's seriousness as misplaced. One is strict about time and loose about money; the other is the reverse — and each privately thinks the other is the careless one. The repair is naming the standard out loud instead of assuming it is obvious.
Saturn|Saturn.facing: They stand at opposite ends of the same demand. What one treats as a duty you do not question, the other treats as the thing you must get free of — and each feels the pull of the other's stance. Over years they can hold each other's limits better than either holds their own, but only if neither tries to win the point.

Saturn|Uranus.fused: One person's rules land exactly where the other needs air, so every limit is felt at once and taken personally. Nothing is neutral — a small request about timekeeping can become a question about whether either of you can breathe. Handled well it makes you both honest about what is actually required; handled badly it is a lock and a lockpick in the same drawer.
Saturn|Uranus.easy: The serious one gives shape without it feeling like a cage, and the free one moves about without it feeling like abandonment. Structure and space take turns instead of fighting for the same hour. It works so quietly that you may forget most couples argue about this constantly.
Saturn|Uranus.friction: The one who takes commitments seriously reads sudden changes of plan as unreliability; the one who needs room reads a set schedule as being managed. The same row returns in different costumes — the diary, the phone, the visit to family. It softens when the free one promises fewer things and actually keeps them, and the serious one leaves some evenings genuinely unclaimed.
Saturn|Uranus.facing: There is real attraction across this gap: the steady one is drawn to someone who refuses to be pinned down, and the restless one is drawn to someone who does not blow away. The tension is just as real, and it never fully resolves — it becomes a negotiation you both get better at. Expect to be each other's brake and each other's open window, sometimes in the same afternoon.

Neptune|Saturn.fused: The serious one's standards sit right on top of the other's dreams, and each colours the other. At best an idea gets built rather than only admired; at worst the dream is inspected until nothing lovely is left of it, or the standard quietly bends around a fantasy. Watch which of the two is doing the deciding.
Neptune|Saturn.easy: One brings the picture, the other brings the timetable, and neither treats the other's contribution as decoration. Vague hopes turn into actual plans without much of a fight. The only danger is assuming this is normal and forgetting to be glad of it.
Neptune|Saturn.friction: The one who deals in facts keeps puncturing the other's picture, meaning to be helpful; the one who imagines keeps hearing "no" as "you are being silly". Left alone it becomes a habit of not sharing an idea until it is safe, which is a slow loss. Try treating a half-formed idea as a draft that is not being marked yet.
Neptune|Saturn.facing: Strong pull: the plain one is fed by the other's ability to picture something better, and the dreamer wants somebody solid to lean the dream against. Across the gap lives disappointment — one feels dragged down, the other feels let down by reality. The gap is real, and pretending otherwise is what does the damage.

Pluto|Saturn.fused: One person's rules land on what the other absolutely will not release, and together they make something very hard to shift. When you are both right, this is unbreakable loyalty and enormous staying power. When you are both wrong, nothing moves for years and neither of you can quite say why.
Pluto|Saturn.easy: The serious one's limits and the other's deep hold work as one force rather than two. You can stick with a difficult thing — a business, a treatment, a child's hard year — long after most people would have stopped. Because it takes no effort, you will need some other way of noticing when persistence has quietly become stubbornness.
Pluto|Saturn.friction: One wants the matter settled and filed; the other cannot stop returning to it. Each reads the other badly — a cold refusal to discuss, versus an inability to move on. It clears only when the closed one agrees to one proper conversation and the holding one agrees it will be the last for now.
Pluto|Saturn.facing: Two kinds of iron facing each other. One holds the line by shutting down, the other by never letting go, and each recognises real strength in the other — which is exactly why neither steps back. Struggles here are slow and quiet rather than loud; the way out is deciding together what you are both actually defending.

Rahu|Saturn.fused: The serious one's caution sits directly on the other's hunger for whatever has not been tried, and both get louder. It can produce genuine ambition — an appetite for something new that also does the boring paperwork. It can also produce a strange stop-go rhythm where you lunge at something and freeze on the same day.
Rahu|Saturn.easy: The one who wants to try something new finds an ally rather than a wet blanket, and the careful one gets drawn into things they would never have started alone. New ventures here tend to survive their first year. It is easy to take for granted how unusual it is to have both nerve and patience in one partnership.
Rahu|Saturn.friction: One says "not yet, we are not ready"; the other has already signed up. The recurring snag is timing rather than direction — you often want the same thing, six months apart. Agreeing a date in advance works far better than arguing about the principle.
Rahu|Saturn.facing: A real pull across a real gap: the cautious one is fascinated by the other's appetite, and the appetite is steadied by the other's weight. Each also suspects the other is the problem — too slow, too greedy. Long term this is one of the more productive tensions, provided neither tries to convert the other.

Ketu|Saturn.fused: One person's sense of duty lands on the other's readiness to walk away, and the mix goes quiet fast. Together you can end things cleanly that other people drag out for years. The risk is a chill nobody names: one withdrawing on principle, the other simply no longer minding.
Ketu|Saturn.easy: The serious one's limits and the other's loose grip fit without effort. What must be done gets done, and what has finished is allowed to finish. This is a rare and useful combination, and mostly you will notice it as an absence of drama.
Ketu|Saturn.friction: The one with the duty keeps carrying something the other put down long ago, and quietly resents it. The other keeps being told they are cold when, to them, the thing is simply over. The way through is separating the obligation itself from the feelings about it, then deciding out loud which of you is actually responsible.
Ketu|Saturn.facing: One holds on out of principle, the other releases out of instinct, and each sees something they want in the other — relief on one side, backbone on the other. The gap shows up around endings: jobs, friendships, family ties. Expect to argue less about whether to stop and more about what stopping is supposed to mean.

Uranus|Uranus.fused: Both of them need room in exactly the same way, and they know it about each other without discussion. Nobody polices anybody, plans stay loose, and neither takes independence personally. The catch is that with two people this unbound, nothing holds them together except wanting to be there — which is either beautiful or precarious, depending on the week.
Uranus|Uranus.easy: They need freedom at compatible sizes, so one's night out is not the other's crisis. Space gets given before it has to be asked for. It costs so little that they may both assume every couple manages it.
Uranus|Uranus.friction: Both want room, but not at the same times or in the same shape. One disappears just as the other has finally come home, and each ends up feeling abandoned by a person who thought they were being generous. Diaries help more here than declarations.
Uranus|Uranus.facing: Each is drawn to the other's independence and unsettled by it in equal measure. Freedom becomes the thing they pull on: one goes further out, and the other, keeping pace, goes further still. It works when they treat it as one shared question — how much room do we need — rather than two competing demands.

Neptune|Uranus.fused: One person's need for room lands on the other's picture of how things ought to be, and the two fuse into one restless idea. You can talk each other into anything — a different city, a different life — and it will feel like a vision rather than a whim. Keep at least one dull, practical thing anchored while you do it.
Neptune|Uranus.easy: The free one is not threatened by the other's dreaming, and the dreamer does not need the free one to stay put in order to feel loved. Ideas and space feed each other. It flows so easily you might stop testing either of them.
